problem.duplicate_id: Two objects share the same identifier.
problem.duplicate_name: Another one already has this name.
problem.invalid_ha_state: Choose one of the Home Assistant armed states.
problem.siren_out_of_range: {field}: between 1 and 900 seconds (the EN 50131 reference for external sounders).
problem.retention_out_of_range: {field}: keep each category between 1 and 3650 days. To keep nothing, switch the category off.
problem.supervision_out_of_range: {field}: between 60 seconds and 7 days, or empty for off.
problem.scenario_without_areas: A scenario must arm at least one area.
problem.unknown_area: The chosen area does not exist.
problem.unsupported_domain: This kind of entity cannot be a zone.
problem.trigger_domain: Event and tag entities need an event trigger, and only they can have one.
problem.fault_state_as_trigger: Unavailable and unknown are faults, not triggers. They always block arming.
problem.eq_hysteresis: An equality trigger has no hysteresis.
problem.event_type_required: Choose which event type triggers the zone.
problem.event_type_not_allowed: A tag has only one event, the scan: leave the type empty.
problem.key_action_required: A key zone needs an action.
problem.key_scenario_required: Choose the scenario this key arms.
problem.key_always_on: A key zone commands; it cannot be always on.
problem.key_action_not_allowed: Only key zones have a key action.
problem.always_on_must_be_instant: An always-on zone fires at once: no entry delay applies.
problem.auto_bypass_needs_bypassable: Automatic exclusion needs a zone that may be excluded.
problem.hold_needs_arm_after_closing: The wait limit applies only to “arm after closing”.
problem.area_not_disarmed: This area is not disarmed. Disarm it before changing what protects it.
problem.scenario_active: This scenario is running. Disarm before editing it.
problem.trigger_not_confirmed: Confirm the trigger states against the real sensor first.
problem.not_found: It no longer exists. Reload the page.
problem.area_has_zones: Move or delete this area's zones first.
problem.area_in_scenario: Remove this area from its scenarios first.
problem.scenario_in_use: A key zone arms this scenario. Change the key zone first.
problem.follows_needs_follower: Only a follower zone can follow other zones.
problem.follows_not_delayed: A follower can follow only delayed intrusion zones.
problem.request_failed: Home Assistant did not accept the request ({detail}). Nothing was changed. Reload the page and try again.
problem.area_has_groups: A verification group is shown in this area. Move or delete it first.
problem.zone_in_group: This zone is a member of a verification group. Remove it from the group first.
problem.zone_is_cross_partner: Another zone uses this one for cross-zone verification. Change that zone first.
problem.cross_zone_window_mismatch: Both zones of this pair point at each other with different windows. Give them the same window.
problem.group_members: A group needs at least two different members.
problem.group_member_invalid: Only existing intrusion zones can be members.
problem.group_threshold: The threshold must be at least 2 and no more than the number of members.
problem.zone_in_two_groups: A zone can belong to one group or cross-zone pair only, or it would count twice.
problem.technical_always_on: A technical zone is always live: it must be always on.
problem.chime_always_on: An always-on zone is always watched, so it can never chime.
problem.chime_target_invalid: The chime plays on media players and sirens only.
problem.chime_tts_required: Speaking the zone name needs a text-to-speech entity.
problem.chime_sound_required: Media players need a sound to play: set the media to play.
problem.quiet_hours_incomplete: Quiet hours need both a start and an end.
problem.unknown_profile: That response profile does not exist.
problem.camera_dir_invalid: Use a folder inside the configuration directory, never www: it is served without authentication.
problem.severity_out_of_range: Severity is a number from 1 to 10.
problem.moments_required: Choose at least one moment for this action.
problem.too_many_conditions: An action carries at most two conditions.
problem.empty_window: A window that starts when it ends never applies.
problem.condition_entity_invalid: Choose an entity and the state to compare it with.
problem.unknown_variable: {field} uses a variable that does not exist.
problem.notify_service_required: Choose a notify service or notify entity.
problem.service_required: Give a domain and a service.
problem.data_invalid: Service data must be a mapping.
problem.entity_required: Choose at least one entity for {field}.
problem.entity_domain: {field} points at an entity this action cannot use.
problem.camera_mode_invalid: Choose a snapshot or a recording.
problem.brightness_out_of_range: Brightness is a number from 0 to 255.
problem.not_a_foyer_backup: That file is not a Foyer configuration backup.
problem.backup_version_unsupported: That backup was written by a newer version of Foyer than this one. Update Foyer first.
problem.profile_in_use: Something still uses this profile. Point it elsewhere first.
problem.code_in_use: {field}: that code already belongs to somebody.
problem.ha_user_already_linked: That Home Assistant account is already linked to another user.
problem.window_inverted: {field}: the end is before the start.
problem.exemption_needs_a_linked_account: The exemption needs a linked Home Assistant account: without one, nothing can identify this person without a code.
problem.no_user_allowed: {field}: a scenario nobody may use cannot be armed. Leave it open to everyone instead.
problem.user_holds_a_key: A key zone is attributed to this user. Change the zone first.
problem.user_in_scenario: A scenario names this user. Change the scenario first.
problem.not_permitted: You are not allowed to do that.
problem.user_not_valid: That code is not valid at the moment.
problem.locked_out: Too many wrong codes. This channel is locked for now.
problem.area_not_allowed: You are not allowed to act on that area.
problem.scenario_not_allowed: You are not allowed to use that scenario.
problem.ref_required: A keypad needs the identifier it puts in its own messages.
problem.duplicate_ref: Another device already answers to that identifier. Two keypads sharing one would share a lockout counter and a log row that names neither.
problem.keypad_has_no_entity: A keypad is shared and carries a code: it has no entity and no owner. A tag or a remote is the other kind.
problem.tag_has_no_ref: A tag carries no code, so it must not answer to a name anybody could type: leave the identifier empty.
problem.tag_entity_required: Choose the tag or event entity a scan arrives on.
problem.tag_needs_a_user: A tag is somebody's: choose whose. Possession is the credential, so this is the only identity it has — and a tag nobody owns is a shared code with no code.
problem.scenario_required: Choose the scenario this device arms.
problem.topic_invalid: A topic has no wildcard (+ or #) and no empty level. Leave it empty for the default.
problem.topics_identical: The command and state topics must differ, or Foyer would answer its own messages.
problem.device_not_registered: That device is not registered here.
problem.user_holds_a_tag: This person owns a tag or a remote. Change the device first.
problem.unknown_attachment: This attachment is not one Foyer knows how to send.
problem.unsupported_battery_domain: A battery must be a sensor reporting a percentage, or a battery binary sensor where “on” means low.
problem.battery_is_zone_entity: That is the zone’s own entity, not its battery.
problem.walk_test_out_of_range: The walk test timeout must be between 1 and 60 minutes. It cannot be switched off.
problem.contact_in_use: An action still notifies this contact. Edit the profile first.
problem.contact_without_channels: Give this contact at least one channel: a contact nobody can reach is a step that reaches nobody.
problem.escalation_kind_invalid: Only a notification can be an escalation step.
problem.escalation_moment_invalid: An escalation step answers an alarm or a technical alarm: those are the two that can be acknowledged.
problem.escalation_offset_out_of_range: Put this step between 0 and 3600 seconds from the start.
problem.notify_target_ambiguous: Choose contacts or a service, not both.
problem.notify_target_required: Say who this notification reaches: contacts, or a notification service.
problem.unknown_channel: That contact no longer has this channel.
problem.rule_without_people: Choose at least one person for this rule to watch.
problem.rule_entity_invalid: A rule watches people: choose a person or a device tracker.
problem.rule_entity_required: Choose the entity this rule watches.
problem.rule_state_required: Say which state the entity has to hold.
problem.rule_without_areas: Choose at least one area to disarm.
problem.rule_only_perimeter: Every area named here is a perimeter area, which a rule never disarms. The rule would do nothing.
problem.rule_countdown_without_contacts: A countdown needs somebody to announce it to, or there is nobody to cancel it.
problem.weekday_invalid: Choose valid days of the week.
problem.window_incomplete: Set both ends of the window, or neither.
problem.rule_out_of_range: That value is outside the range this setting allows.
problem.health_out_of_range: That value is outside the range this setting allows.
problem.health_entity_invalid: That is not an entity id.
problem.mains_states_required: Say which state of that entity means the mains has failed.
problem.watchdog_url_required: A watchdog that is switched on needs an http or https URL.
problem.watchdog_timeout_too_long: The timeout must be shorter than the interval between pings.
problem.duplicate_radio_entry: Another radio already uses that integration.
problem.radio_entry_required: Choose which integration this radio is.
problem.coordinator_required: Name the coordinator entity, or switch this radio off. Without it Foyer cannot tell interference from a dead coordinator, and will not guess.

entry_mode_hint.instant: Triggers the alarm at once when the area is armed.
entry_mode_hint.delayed: Starts the entry delay: the way in, such as the front door.
entry_mode_hint.follower: Inherits a running entry delay — its own area's, or one opened by a zone it follows; instant otherwise. It is the zone along the way in: the hallway you cross after opening the front door.

arm_policy_hint.block: Arming fails and names this zone.
arm_policy_hint.auto_bypass: Excluded and announced; it rejoins by itself once closed.
arm_policy_hint.arm_after_closing: Arming waits, after the exit delay, until it closes. It fails if it stays open too long.
arm_policy_hint.ignore: Arms regardless. It fires the next time it opens.

overview.no_codes_warning: Nobody holds a code yet, so nothing asks for one: anyone with access to Home Assistant can disarm. Create a user with a code on the Users page and it stops being true.
overview.memory_banner: Alarm memory in {area}: {zones}. Disarm the area to clear it.
overview.scenario_hint: Choosing a scenario arms its areas. While armed, it switches: areas not in the new one are disarmed.
overview.force_arm_hint: Excludes the zones above and records the arming as forced.
overview.technical_banner: Technical alarm: {zones}. A separate channel: arming does not affect it and disarming does not clear it. It clears once acknowledged and back to normal.
overview.incident_acknowledged: Acknowledged — it closes once every area is disarmed or armed again
overview.incident_hint: One incident gathers every zone of one alarm. Disarming also acknowledges it.
overview.memory_banner_plain: Alarm memory in {area}. Disarm the area to clear it.
overview.low_battery: Armed, but these zones are on a low battery: {zones}. Exclude one from this arming, or replace the cell.

areas.title: Areas
areas.reports_as_hint: What voice assistants and HomeKit see. Changes nothing about behaviour.
areas.entry_hint: For zones that do not set their own.
areas.exit_hint: Time to leave after arming, unless the scenario sets its own.
areas.perimeter_hint: The outer defence ring. An automatic rule never disarms a perimeter area, whatever the rule says (§9.4).

zones.title: Zones
zones.no_areas: Create an area first: every zone belongs to one.
zones.entity_hint: Any sensor, contact, cover, lock, switch, person, event or tag.
zones.state_hint: Normally-closed and normally-open contacts behave in opposite ways. Open the door or walk past and watch the state.
zones.hysteresis_hint: How far back it must go before it counts as normal again.
zones.attribute_hint: Read this attribute instead of the state.
zones.tag_hint: A tag fires every time it is scanned.
zones.event_hint: Only this event triggers the zone.
zones.confirm: I have checked this against the real sensor
zones.confirm_hint: A wrong choice is a zone that never fires, found out during a break-in.
zones.type_hint: A preset: it fills the fields below, which all stay editable.
zones.hold_hint: Empty: the global default. Counted from the end of the exit delay.
zones.supervision_hint: Silent longer than this is a fault; any report counts, even without a change. Set it longer than this sensor's own reporting interval. Empty: off, which is the default and right for sensors that report only when they change.
zones.bypassable_hint: Needed for automatic or forced exclusion.
zones.allow_faulted_hint: Arming proceeds even if this zone cannot be seen. Leave off unless you know why.
zones.enabled_hint: A disabled zone is ignored completely.
zones.key_hint: A key arms or disarms as a person would. It never alarms.
zones.area_armed: This zone's area is armed: changes are refused until it is disarmed.
zones.follows_hint: Its own area's entry delay always counts. Tick the delayed zones of other areas whose entry delay it should also inherit, such as the front door for a hall sensor in an interior area.
zones.fire_statement: Foyer is not a fire alarm system. A smoke or gas detector connected to Home Assistant does not replace certified, interconnected smoke alarms.
zones.technical_hint: A technical zone raises the technical alarm whatever the areas are doing. It never triggers an area and disarming never clears it. Save it while the detector is quiet: a detector already detecting when saved counts as its starting point and alarms only once it has returned to normal and detects again.
zones.cross_zone_hint: Another zone that confirms this one within the window. Each still alarms on its own; when both detect, the pair is recorded as confirmed. Set it on either zone.
zones.trigger_count_hint: How many times it must detect within the window before it alarms. 1: at once. Only detections that would alarm at once are counted: opening the entry route is not.
zones.chime_hint: Plays the chime when it opens while its area is not armed.
zones.in_group: Member of the verification group {group}. Change it on the Verification groups page.
zones.bypass_hint: An excluded zone does not alarm. Without a duration it comes back when the area is disarmed; with one it comes back on its own, and says so.
zones.silent_hint: The response runs without the sounders the settings list.
zones.profile_hint: Read only when this zone alarms. Empty: the area's profile.
zones.battery_hint: For diagnostics and the low-battery warning. A low battery warns and never blocks arming; an entity that cannot be read at all is a fault and does block.

scenarios.title: Scenarios
scenarios.shared_mode: Shared with another scenario: the master cannot arm this mode.
scenarios.mode_hint: Several scenarios may share one; the master then refuses that mode and the scenario is chosen here.
scenarios.exit_hint: Empty: each area's own exit delay.
scenarios.siren_hint: At most 900 s. Empty: the global setting.
scenarios.areas_hint: Only these are armed. Switching to another scenario disarms the areas it does not list.

card.no_entity: Set an entity: a Foyer alarm_control_panel.
card.layout_full: Full — areas, scenarios, countdown and what blocks arming
card.editor_hint: The keypad and badge layouts need a code to be useful; the keypad appears once somebody holds one.
card.layout_badge: Badge — state only, for a dashboard of your own

help.global_toggle: Show or hide every help panel

overview.title: What this page shows
overview.intro: The live state of the alarm. It updates by itself; every button acts at once.

area.text: Arms and disarms on its own. Its button arms only that area.

master.text: Derived from the areas: armed if any is. Disarm here disarms everything.

scenario.text: Arms a set of areas. Chosen while armed, it switches.

not_ready.text: Open, faulted or excluded zones. Faults block arming unless the zone allows it.

memory.text: Stays after the sounders stop, until someone disarms.

technical.text: Smoke, gas, water: its own channel. Disarming does not clear it; acknowledge it.

incident.text: Every zone of one alarm, acknowledged once.

areas.title: What an area is
areas.intro: A group of zones armed together, with its own state and alarm panel entity. Group by what you arm together — perimeter, interior day, interior night — not by room: that is what makes "dog at home, perimeter only" possible.

own_state.text: Each area arms, delays and alarms independently.

entry.text: Longer gives you more time to disarm, and an intruder the same.

exit.text: Zones still open when it ends are handled by their own arm policy.

reports_as.text: What Home Assistant, HomeKit and voice assistants see. Behaviour is unchanged.

zones.title: What a zone is
zones.intro: One Home Assistant entity plus alarm semantics. The type is only a preset; the engine reads the fields.

trigger.text: Which state means an alarm. Get it wrong and the zone never fires.

type.text: Fills the fields below. Every field stays editable.

entry_mode.text: Instant alarms at once; delayed starts the entry delay; follower inherits it, and is instant when there is nothing to inherit.

arm_policy.text: Block names the zone; exclude lets it rejoin once closed; ignore arms anyway.

hold.text: Waits for the door you leave by. Fails if it stays open past the limit.

always_on.text: Fires even when disarmed. Tamper and panic are always on.

supervision.text: A sensor silent too long is a fault, never “all quiet”.

verification.text: Cross-zone and activations needed cut false alarms; a group does it for several zones.

scenarios.title: What a scenario is
scenarios.intro: A named set of areas to arm together. Create as many as the house needs.

areas.text: Exactly these are armed by it.

reports_master.text: The mode HomeKit and voice assistants see. A mode shared by two scenarios cannot be armed from the master.

switching.text: Choosing another scenario while armed disarms the areas it does not list.

exit_override.text: Replaces each area's own for this scenario.

siren.text: A night scenario may sound for less. Never more than 900 s.

groups.title: What a verification group is
groups.intro: A group confirms an alarm when at least N of its member zones detect within a window: the strongest tool against false alarms in large spaces. A zone's cross-zone field is the same engine, as a 2-of-2 group.

threshold.text: How many members, within how long. A longer window is easier to satisfy.

members.text: Any intrusion zone, in any area. Opening the entry route never counts.

suppress.text: Off by default: each member still alarms alone. On: nothing until the group is satisfied.

derived.text: Cross-zone pairs, shown here and edited on the zone.

settings.title: What these settings do
settings.intro: Settings that apply to the whole installation: the chime, and where every response chain ends.

targets.text: Where the chime sounds. Nothing chimes until one is set.

mode.text: A sound, or the zone's name spoken, which tells you what opened.

quiet.text: No chime inside this window. A target may carry a window of its own.

during_exit.text: Whether zones chime while their area counts down to armed.

response.text: The profile everything inherits, the one the technical channel uses, and what a silent zone keeps quiet.

retention.text: Per category, in days. A category switched off writes nothing from now on; rows already written stay until their days are up.

backup.text: A JSON file of the whole configuration. Restoring it goes through the same validation as any edit, and is refused while an area it would change is armed.

language.text: The language of what Foyer sends out — notifications, the spoken zone name. This panel already follows each Home Assistant user's own language.

profiles.title: What a response profile is
profiles.intro: A profile is a named list of actions: what happens, when, and under which conditions. The area is the unit of response; a zone's own profile is read only for its own alarm, which is what makes a verification group's graduated response work.

inheritance.text: Zone, then area, then scenario, then the global default. The page shows the effective profile and where it comes from.

moments.text: One action can answer several moments. Some moments arrive with a later phase and are marked.

conditions.text: At most two per action, combined with and or or. More than that belongs in a Home Assistant automation.

severity.text: Only decides which escalation an incident adopts when profiles of different strength contribute to it.

silent.text: A zone marked silent runs its response without the action kinds the settings name.

log.title: What is recorded, and for how long
log.intro: Stored in Foyer's own database rather than Home Assistant's recorder, whose ten-day purge would quietly destroy a thirty-day requirement. Every row records what happened, where, and through which channel.

category.text: Groups rows by kind. Each category is switched on or off, and kept for its own number of days, in Settings.

zone_disarmed.text: Off by default: one motion sensor produces thousands of rows a day and buries everything that matters. Switch it on while diagnosing, and off again afterwards.

incident.text: A real break-in trips several zones. They share one incident id, so a night reads as one story rather than as scattered rows.

user.text: The person is written into the row rather than referenced, so deleting a user later does not erase the history of what they did. Users arrive in the next phase; until then rows carry the channel.

export.text: CSV or JSON of exactly the rows the filters above are showing — not of the whole database.

users.title: What this page decides
users.intro: Everyone has their own code, because a shared one makes “who disarmed at 03:14?” unanswerable. Codes are stored as hashes and checked in the backend only: a card is a keypad that transmits a code, never something that decides.

own_code.text: A code may not belong to two people. Change one and the log keeps every action the old one signed.

policy.text: Which operations ask for a code. An area or a scenario can ask for more; where they disagree, the one that asks wins.

identified.term: Where a code can be skipped
identified.text: Only on channels that already know who you are. On a shared keypad the code is the identity, so the exemption cannot apply there.

duress.text: Disarms exactly as the ordinary code does and raises a silent alarm. Nothing the person at the keypad can see is different.

lockout.text: Repeated wrong codes shut that keypad for a while, longer each time. It is also an event a response profile can answer: somebody guessing at a keypad is a tamper signal.

scope.text: A code can be limited to some areas or scenarios, and can stop working on a date — which is what makes a guest code a guest code.

devices.title: What this page decides
devices.intro: Any device that can call a service or publish to MQTT can arm this system and receives structured feedback for its LEDs, beeps and display. Keypad models change every few months; this contract does not. A device must be declared here before it may command anything.

declared.text: A device that is not on this page is refused, whatever code it brings, and the refusal is recorded and shown.

device_id.text: Recorded on every event, and what the lockout counts attempts against. Give each keypad its own.

identifies.text: A personal tag or badge identifies who acted, and needs no code. A shared keypad cannot, so the code is the only identity it has.

topics.text: Configurable, because people run more than one site against one broker and have a hierarchy they will not restructure.

detail.text: It is retained on a broker that is often shared, so it starts at the least a keypad needs and opens up only if you ask.

last_result.text: Lets a keypad distinguish a wrong code from arming blocked by an open window, instead of failing silently.

test.title: What this page proves
test.intro: The point of an alarm you configured yourself is that you can check it before trusting it. The first two tabs only look: the table says what every zone is doing right now, and the simulator says what the house would do about it without doing any of it. The last two act: the walk test really arms the house and holds the response back, and the action test really sounds the siren.

trigger_column.text: Whether Foyer counts the zone as triggered right now, read through that zone's own trigger. A normally-closed contact alarms on “off”, so the raw state beside it is not the answer.

blocks.text: Whether this zone would stop its area arming, and which of the two reasons: a fault to fix, or a window to close.

battery.text: A low battery warns and never blocks: a contact at 15 % still sees. A battery entity that cannot be read at all is a fault, and that one does block.

nothing_runs.text: The simulator runs the same engine the alarm runs and throws the result away. No siren, no notification, no change to what is armed.

clock.text: An action limited to 22:00–07:00 runs or does not run depending on this field. Set it to the hour you actually want to check.

skipped.term: Why an action did not run
skipped.text: Every action of the profile is listed, including the ones that were skipped, with the reason: a condition, a silent zone, a siren already sounding, or a delay still holding the rest of the sequence.

inherited.text: Zone, group, area, scenario or the global default. If a response looks arbitrary, this line is usually why.

walk_never.text: This is the finding, not the ones that did. A zone with no detection is either a door nobody opened or a PIR pointing at the wrong wall, and only you can tell which.

walk_timeout.text: Every detection pushes the timeout back so a large house can be walked in one pass, and an absolute cap ends it whatever happens. Neither can be switched off: while it runs, a real intrusion produces nothing.

walk_live.text: 24h, tamper, technical and panic zones respond in full, alarm included. A walk test never silences a smoke detector.

action_real.text: That is what makes it worth having: the failure it prevents is discovering during the emergency that the emergency channel was misconfigured. It asks first, and every run is in the log as a test rather than as an alarm.

contacts.title: What this page decides
contacts.intro: Escalation targets people, not services. Home Assistant already provides the transports — push, SMS, voice, messaging — so what is configured here is the order, the timing, and what counts as somebody having taken notice.

order.text: Tried highest first. Put the channel that survives a cut internet connection somewhere in the list, not at the bottom.

quiet.text: Only what is loud enough reaches this contact inside the window. It never suppresses an alarm to the whole household.

linked.text: Lets an acknowledgement from a phone be attributed to a person in the log.

step.text: A notification with a time on it, on the profile that answers the alarm. The policy stops the instant anyone acknowledges.

acknowledge.text: Four paths stop the policy, and each records who answered and how.

webhook.text: An unauthenticated URL that stops an alarm. Off until you switch it on, and worth giving to nothing but the voice provider.

test.text: Really sends. Use it — an untested emergency channel is one you discover during the emergency.

rules.title: What this page decides
rules.intro: A closed rule model, not an automation engine: four triggers, three actions, an active window and three guards. Rules act as a user would, so everything they do is logged with the rule's name against the auto_rule channel — and everything a guard stopped is logged too, because “why did it not arm last night?” is a question people ask.

trigger.text: Absence and entity state are conditions that stay true, so a rule a guard blocked acts as soon as the guard clears. A time or an arrival happens once: blocked, that occurrence is missed.

guards.text: Each one is a reason not to act. They are evaluated again when the countdown ends, because two minutes is long enough for somebody to come home.

grace.text: A notification with a Cancel button before the rule acts. Nobody presses anything and it happens; somebody presses Cancel and the rule waits until its condition becomes true again.

suspension.text: Holds rules back until a date and time, or for one occurrence. It is not a configuration change: it expires on its own.

visitor.text: The same suspension with a name on it. Mechanically identical; the difference is that the log still says why in six months.

disarming.text: Off until you turn it on, and never on a perimeter area. A scenario switch that would leave an armed area disarmed counts as disarming.

next.text: What is scheduled, not what will certainly happen: the guards are evaluated at the moment the rule acts, and the log says which one stopped it.

health.title: What system health watches
health.intro: An alarm that cannot tell you it has stopped working has stopped working. This page is the answer to the four failures that silently defeat a DIY alarm: the power goes out, the notification channel breaks, the radio goes quiet, or Home Assistant dies. None of it is an intrusion, and none of it ever reaches the alarm panel.

mains.text: Name the entity and which of its states means failure. A power cut is announced at once and is never a quiet night.

channels.text: Checked periodically and after every real send. A broken channel is announced over a different one.

watchdog.text: If Home Assistant dies the pings stop and the service you chose raises the alarm. Foyer also reports when it cannot reach it.

payload.text: Off. On, the ping says how many areas are armed, which tells a third party when the house is empty.

radio.text: Zones are grouped by the integration they come from. Interference is suspected, never proven.

coordinator.text: Without one, nothing is raised on that radio: it is what separates jamming from a dead coordinator.

diagnostics.text: Home Assistant's own download button, with everything personal removed and entity ids replaced.

device_rejected.title: Foyer: unknown device
device_rejected.message: A device calling itself “{device}” tried to command the alarm and is not one of this installation's arming devices. Nothing was changed. Add it under Arming devices if it is yours.

armed_area.title: Foyer: armed
armed_area.message: {area} armed on its own, outside any scenario.

arm_failed.title: Foyer: arming failed
arm_failed.message: {area} did not arm. Still open or in fault: {zones}. It is disarmed.

zone_bypassed.title: Foyer: zone excluded
zone_bypassed.message: {zone} was open at arming and is excluded. It rejoins by itself once it closes.

zone_rejoined.title: Foyer: zone back in
zone_rejoined.message: {zone} has closed and is protected again.

entry_started.title: Foyer: entry delay
entry_started.message: {zone} opened in {area}. Disarm before the delay ends.

siren_cutoff.title: Foyer: sounders stopped
siren_cutoff.message: The alarm in {area} is over; the area is back to its previous state. Disarm to clear the alarm memory.

zone_fault.title: Foyer: zone fault
zone_fault.message: Zone {zone} in {area} cannot be seen. It blocks arming until it is seen again.

ha_restarted.title: Foyer: back online
ha_restarted.message: Foyer was not running for a while. The house was not protected during that time.

technical_raised.title: Foyer: TECHNICAL ALARM
technical_raised.message: {zone} in {area} detects a technical alarm. Disarming does not clear it: acknowledge it once it is safe. Foyer is not a fire alarm system.

technical_acknowledged.title: Foyer: technical alarm acknowledged
technical_acknowledged.message: Acknowledged: {zones}. It clears once back to normal.

technical_cleared.title: Foyer: technical alarm cleared
technical_cleared.message: {zone} is back to normal and acknowledged.

chime_switched.title: Foyer: chime
chime_switched.message: The chime was switched on or off.

code_rejected.title: Foyer: code rejected
code_rejected.message: A wrong code was entered on {channel}.

lockout.title: Foyer: locked out
lockout.message: Too many wrong codes on {channel}. That channel is locked.

walk_test_started.title: Foyer: walk test
walk_test_started.message: A walk test has started. Response actions are inhibited.

walk_test_ended.title: Foyer: walk test over
walk_test_ended.message: The walk test has ended. The system responds normally again.

escalation_exhausted.title: Foyer: nobody answered
escalation_exhausted.message: The escalation reached its last step without an acknowledgement.

duress.title: Duress code used
duress.message: {user} disarmed {area} with a duress code at {time}.

action_tested.title: Foyer: action test
action_tested.message: This is a test. Nothing has happened in the house.

escalation_skipped.title: Foyer: notifications were not sent
escalation_skipped.message: Home Assistant was down when these escalation steps fell due, so they were not sent.

auto_pending.title: Foyer: acting in {seconds} s
auto_pending.message: Rule “{rule}” is about to act. Cancel to stop it.

auto_pending_arm.title: Foyer: arming in {seconds} s
auto_pending_arm.message: Nobody seems to be in, so “{rule}” will arm {scenario}. Cancel to stop it.

auto_pending_disarm.title: Foyer: disarming in {seconds} s
auto_pending_disarm.message: Rule “{rule}” will disarm. Cancel to stop it.

auto_pending_switch.title: Foyer: changing scenario in {seconds} s
auto_pending_switch.message: Rule “{rule}” will switch to {scenario}. Cancel to stop it.

auto_cancelled.title: Foyer: cancelled
auto_cancelled.message: The automatic action of “{rule}” was cancelled.

auto_suspension_cleared.title: Foyer: suspension over
auto_suspension_cleared.message: The suspension of automatic arming has ended.

auto_arming_switched.title: Foyer: automatic rules
auto_arming_switched.message: Automatic rules were switched on or off.

system_power_lost.title: Foyer: mains power lost
system_power_lost.message: The house has lost mains power. Everything that needs the internet stops when the router does: if you are reading this, the message got out.

system_power_restored.title: Foyer: mains power back
system_power_restored.message: Mains power is back after {seconds} s.

notification_channel_down.title: Foyer: a notification channel is broken
notification_channel_down.message: {contact} cannot be reached through {service}. This message went out over a different channel, because warning you about a dead channel over the dead channel would tell you nothing.

watchdog_unreachable.title: Foyer: watchdog unreachable
watchdog_unreachable.message: The external watchdog has not answered {failures} times running. Nothing that needs the internet would reach you either.

watchdog_recovered.title: Foyer: watchdog reachable again
watchdog_recovered.message: The external watchdog is answering again.

rf_interference_suspected.title: Foyer: radio interference suspected
rf_interference_suspected.message: {count} of {of} zones on {radio} went quiet at once and the coordinator is still answering. Suspected, not proven: a coordinator crash, a firmware update or a power cut to a room of routers looks the same. Not used, because they are on that radio: {skipped}

radio_coordinator_down.title: Foyer: radio coordinator unreachable
radio_coordinator_down.message: The coordinator of {radio} cannot be reached, so its {zones} zones are not being watched. This is not interference — it is the coordinator, its power or its network.

radio_coordinator_up.title: Foyer: radio coordinator back
radio_coordinator_up.message: The coordinator of {radio} is answering again.

technical_state.acknowledged: Acknowledged, not back to normal yet

groups.title: Verification groups
groups.from_zone_hint: Cross-zone pairs appear here as 2-of-2 groups. They are edited on the zone, not here.
groups.members_hint: Intrusion zones of any area. A member counts only while its own area is armed, and only detections that would alarm at once count.
groups.suppress_hint: Off: each member still alarms on its own, and the group adds its confirmation. On: members do nothing until the group is satisfied — a single sensor facing a real intruder then produces silence.
groups.window_hint: Seconds within which the members must detect.
groups.no_zones: No intrusion zones available: each zone can be in one group or pair only.

settings.title: Settings
settings.chime_intro: Sounds when a zone with the chime switched on opens while its area is not armed — not merely when the house is disarmed. With only the perimeter armed, an internal door still chimes.
settings.targets_hint: Media players, sirens, and notify services or entities — the phone and Telegram chime too. Each target may carry quiet hours of its own.
settings.no_targets: No media player or siren found.
settings.sound_hint: For media players: a media id or URL, such as media-source://media_source/local/chime.mp3. A siren sounds for one second, if it supports a set duration; otherwise it is skipped.
settings.tts_hint: Used to speak the zone name.
settings.volume_hint: Percent. Empty: leave the player's volume as it is.
settings.quiet_hint: No chime in this window, which may cross midnight. Empty: never quiet.
settings.during_exit_hint: Off: the door you leave by does not chime while the area counts down.
settings.switch_hint: switch.foyer_chime silences it without changing these settings.
settings.response_intro: Where every inheritance chain ends, and what a silent zone keeps quiet.
settings.default_profile_hint: What every area, zone and scenario inherits unless it overrides it.
settings.technical_profile_hint: Smoke, gas and flood answer with this one, whatever the house is doing. Empty: the default profile.
settings.silent_hint: A zone marked silent runs its response without these.
settings.camera_dir_hint: Inside the configuration folder. Never www, which is served without authentication.
settings.defaults_intro: What new areas start with, and the limits that apply to every area.
settings.siren_duration_hint: How long sounders run before stopping. Capped at 900 seconds, the EN 50131 reference for external sounders; a disarm stops them sooner.
settings.arm_hold_hint: How long a zone set to arm after closing may stay open once the exit delay is over. After that, arming fails as if the zone had blocked it.
settings.area_defaults_hint: Only for areas created from now on. Existing areas keep their own delays.
settings.log_intro: Which categories are recorded, and for how long each is kept.
settings.log_rows_hint: Rows already written stay until their days are up, even for a category you switch off.
settings.backup_intro: Nobody who has configured forty zones will do it twice.
settings.backup_hint: The file carries the schema version it was written with. A backup from an older version is brought up to date on restore; one from a newer version is refused rather than half-read.
settings.language_hint: This panel always follows the language of whoever is looking at it. This setting is for what Foyer sends out: notifications, and the zone name the chime speaks.
settings.low_battery_hint: Per cent. Below this a numeric battery counts as low. A battery binary sensor is read by its own “on” instead.
settings.walk_test_hint: Seconds a walk test runs without a detection before it ends itself. Each detection pushes it back, and an absolute cap ends it whatever happens: §5.3 makes the auto-exit mandatory, so there is no value here that switches it off.

condition.midnight_hint: A window may cross midnight: 22:00 to 07:00 is the night.
condition.max: At most two conditions per action. Anything more belongs in a Home Assistant automation subscribed to foyer_event.

profiles.title: Profiles
profiles.intro: A profile is a reusable list of actions. It resolves by inheritance — zone, then area, then scenario, then the global default — which is what stops a house of sixteen zones turning into a configuration matrix.
profiles.severity_hint: Used for one thing only: when several zones join one incident, the incident adopts the escalation of the highest-severity profile among them. It changes nothing when this profile runs alone.
profiles.zone_hint: A zone's own profile is read only for its own alarm. Everything else in this area answers with the area's profile.
profiles.group_hint: What a satisfied group does. Its members keep their own profile: that is what makes the response graduated.
profiles.delay_hint: In seconds. It holds the actions after it in this list, and survives a restart.
profiles.revert_hint: In seconds. Empty: leave it as it is.
profiles.camera_hint: The notification attaches the live picture; the file is written to the camera folder.
profiles.call_service_hint: Anything Foyer does not model natively. Data is JSON.
profiles.escalation_later: An escalation step is a notification with a time on it: give one a step time, and it waits instead of firing at once. Who it reaches lives on the Contacts page.
profiles.future_moment: Raised from a later phase on.
profiles.attach_hint: The live picture goes with the notification, through Home Assistant's authenticated proxy. No file is written.
profiles.attach_hint_telegram: Telegram fetches the picture from outside the house, so a still is written to the camera folder and sent with the message. That folder must be in allowlist_external_dirs.
profiles.pick_or_type: Pick one, or type it: an integration that is not loaded right now is not in the list.
profiles.notify_hint: A notify service (the Companion app, Telegram) or a notify entity. Both work.
profiles.siren_duration_hint: In seconds. It is capped at the siren cutoff, so a siren never outlives the alarm.
profiles.no_contacts: No contacts yet. Add one on the Contacts page to notify a person rather than a service.
profiles.contacts_hint: Who this notification reaches. Choose contacts or a service, never both.
profiles.escalation_hint: Seconds from the start of the escalation. With a time here this notification becomes a step: it waits, and it stops the moment somebody acknowledges.
profiles.escalation_moment_hint: Only an alarm or a technical alarm can be escalated: they are the two that can be acknowledged.

log.categories_hint: Nothing selected means every category. Zone activity while disarmed is only recorded if you switch that category on in Settings.
log.clear_confirm: This deletes every row, for good. The deletion itself is recorded, so the log will not pretend nothing happened.
log.empty: Nothing recorded yet for these filters.
log.truncated: Exported {rows} rows of {total}. Narrow the filters to export the rest.

wizard.title: Finish setting up Foyer
wizard.intro: Foyer is already protecting one zone: the integration created an area, a zone and a scenario when you added it. Four short steps turn that into something that actually guards the house. You can stop at any point and carry on from the pages above.
wizard.no_area: No area found. Add one from the Areas page.
wizard.no_scenario: No scenario found. Add one from the Scenarios page.
wizard.area_text: One area is enough to start. More areas mean more partial arming later — the perimeter alone, or the ground floor with the dog at home.
wizard.exit_hint: How long you have to leave after arming.
wizard.entry_hint: How long you have to disarm after opening a delayed zone. Zones inherit this unless they say otherwise.
wizard.zones_text: You have {have} of {want} zones. Three is plenty to start with; the rest can wait.
wizard.proposed: {entity} reads {state} right now. Foyer proposes a {type} zone, triggered on: {states}.
wizard.confirm_trigger: That is right: this zone is in alarm in those states.
wizard.confirm_hint: This is the one thing Foyer cannot get right on its own. Normally-closed and normally-open contacts behave in opposite ways, and a wrong guess here produces an alarm that never fires — which you would find out at the worst possible moment.
wizard.scenario_text: A scenario is a named preset that arms a chosen set of areas. One that arms everything is enough to start; partial ones come later.
wizard.user_text: Your own code, so the log has somebody to credit from the first day.
wizard.test_text: Prove that a message actually reaches you before you rely on it. This sends one straight through Home Assistant, to the target you pick.
wizard.test_sent: Sent. If nothing arrived, that channel would not have reached you during an alarm either.
wizard.test_hint: Which notifications Foyer sends, and when, is set on the Response profiles page.
wizard.test_message: Foyer Home Defender: this is a test notification.
wizard.user_hint: This person is linked to your Home Assistant account and gets every permission — you are the one setting the system up. Everyone else is added on the Users page, each with their own code.
wizard.user_done: {name} holds a code. From now on disarming asks for one.

code.title: Code
code.wrong: That code is not right. Try again.

code_policy.strictest: Where an area and a scenario disagree, the one that asks for a code wins.
code_policy.inert: Nothing asks for a code yet: no user holds one.

users.title: Users
users.none: No users yet. Until somebody holds a code, anyone who can reach Home Assistant can disarm.
users.not_enforced_hint: No user holds a code, so nothing asks for one. Create a user with a code and the policy below starts applying at once.
users.code_hint: {n} digits, and it may not be anybody else's. Leave it empty to keep the current one.
users.duress_hint: Disarms exactly as the ordinary code does, and raises a silent alarm. Nothing visible changes.
users.linked_hint: Linking a Home Assistant account lets the panel know who is acting without a code being typed.
users.validity_hint: For a guest code: outside this window the code is refused.
users.exempt: Do not ask me for a code where I am identified
users.exempt_hint: Only on channels that identify you by themselves — the Home Assistant UI of your own account.
users.exempt_note: On a shared keypad the code is the identity: the system cannot know who is typing until they type. The exemption never applies there. And a tablet left signed in as you is a disarm anybody passing can press.
users.enabled_hint: A disabled user's code is refused, and their history is kept.
users.policy_hint: Which operations ask for a code. Areas and scenarios can ask for more, never for less.
users.code_length_hint: The same for everybody, because a keypad has to know how many digits to collect. Four digits is ten thousand combinations: it leans entirely on the lockout below.
users.lockout_hint: Each further lockout on the same channel lasts twice as long. The Home Assistant admin path is never locked, so nobody can shut themselves out.

devices.title: Devices
devices.none: No arming device yet. A keypad, a tag or a remote is declared here before it may command anything.
devices.white_list: This list is a white list, not an address book: a device that is not here is refused whatever code it brings. That is what makes the lockout countable, because a caller free to invent a device name is a caller who is never locked out.
devices.kind_hint_keypad: Shared, and carries a code. On a shared keypad the code is the identity, so the per-user exemption can never apply here.
devices.kind_hint_tag: One person's, and carries no code at all: an NFC tag, an RFID badge, a remote.
devices.ref_hint: The name this keypad puts in its own messages, in device_id. It is recorded on every event and is what the lockout counts attempts against, so give each keypad its own.
devices.stolen_tag: A stolen tag arms and disarms without knowing any code.
devices.stolen_tag_hint: Possession is the credential: there is nowhere to type a code on a tag. Keep it as you would keep a key, and give it to somebody you would give a key to. Everything else about that person still applies: what they may do, which areas, and until when.
devices.entity_hint: The tag or event entity a scan arrives on. Scan the tag once with Home Assistant to make it appear.
devices.event_type_hint: For a remote with more than one button: which event counts. Leave it empty for a tag, which has only the scan.
devices.owner_hint: Whose tag this is. This is the whole of its identity, and what the log will say.
devices.enabled_hint: Switched off, it stops commanding, not merely disappearing from this list.
devices.mqtt_note: Keypad models churn every six months; this contract does not. Anything that can publish to a broker can arm this house, and gets structured feedback back for its LEDs and beeps. Everything here is also available as the foyer.* services, for a device that cannot publish MQTT.
devices.mqtt_enabled: Listen and publish on the broker
devices.mqtt_enabled_hint: Off until you switch it on: a broker is often somebody else's machine.
devices.topic_hint: Leave empty for the default, foyer/<install id>/command. People run more than one site against one broker.
devices.detail_hint_minimal: What a keypad needs and nothing else: no scenario name, no area names, no list of open windows.
devices.detail_hint_standard: Adds the active scenario and the state of each area, by name.
devices.detail_hint_full: The contract as written, open zones by name included. Remember what retained means on a shared broker.
devices.retain_hint: Retained, so a keypad that reboots knows the state without asking, and so does anyone else who connects to the broker afterwards.
devices.last_result_hint: last_result is what lets a keypad tell a wrong code from arming blocked by an open window, instead of failing silently.

attachment.companion: Companion app — live picture, no file

diagnostics.title: Live zone state
diagnostics.subtitle: Nothing here is executed
diagnostics.missing: Home Assistant does not have these entities. A zone pointing at an entity that was renamed is a zone that can never fire.

devices.title: Arming devices
devices.subtitle: A keypad cannot block arming, so it has a table of its own

simulator.safe: The simulator calls the same decision engine the alarm calls, with a made-up world and a made-up clock, and then simply never hands the result to whatever would run the sirens.
simulator.scenario_hint: The house is armed with this before anything else happens.
simulator.clock_hint: What a time condition is read against. Empty means now.
simulator.zones_hint: Each one happens this many seconds after the house has finished arming — so zero means “armed, and then this”. The offset is what lets you watch a group fill up, or a second zone join an alarm.
simulator.at: Seconds after the house is armed
simulator.entities_hint: Only the entities an action's conditions read. Leave one empty to use what it really says right now.
simulator.premise_code: This installation asks for a code to arm, and the simulation arms the house before anything else happens — so it asks for one too. Nothing is executed either way.

trace.title: Decision trace
trace.subtitle: What would happen
trace.empty: Choose a scenario and force a zone, then run the simulation.
trace.truncated: Something was still scheduled beyond the end of the run. Nothing after this point was worked out.
trace.low_battery: Armed with a low battery on: {zones}
trace.group: Group “{group}”: {count} of {n} within {window} s → not satisfied
trace.no_profile: ✗ no profile answers this — nothing would run

later.delay: ⏱ the rest of this sequence at {at}

trace.nothing_configured: ✗ nothing is configured for this moment

skip.silent: this zone is silent and suppresses it
skip.already_running: already running for this incident, not restarted
skip.held_by_delay: held back by a delay earlier in the sequence
skip.quiet_hours: every contact it names is inside their quiet hours, or has no channel left

walk.banner: Every response is held back. It ends in {time}, or when you end it. Started by {who}.
walk.card_banner: Every response is held back. Ends in {time}.
walk.badge_title: A walk test is running: every response is held back.
walk.always_on_live: 24h, tamper, technical and panic zones stay fully live. A walk test never silences a smoke detector.
walk.idle: Starting a walk test really arms the house and really reads the sensors. What is held back is the response: no siren, no notification, no light.
walk.active: Walk the house. The table below fills in as zones detect you, and the ones that never do are the finding.
walk.start_sub: Really armed, really reading, nothing answering
walk.explainer: Every area that can arm is armed, and every area is disarmed again when the test ends — except one that was already armed before it started. An area a zone is holding open simply stays out, and is named.
walk.duration_hint: Minutes without a detection before it ends itself. Each detection pushes it back. It can only be shorter than the installation's setting, never longer: the auto-exit cannot be switched off.
walk.never_reacted: {n} zones have not reacted yet. A door nobody opened reads the same as a PIR pointing at the wrong wall — walk them again before you trust the list.
walk.all_reacted: Every zone under test has detected you at least once.
walk.partly_armed: The walk test is running, but these zones kept their area out of it: {zones}. Those areas were never armed, so their zones cannot detect anything.
walk.never_reacted_one: One zone has not reacted yet. A door nobody opened reads the same as a PIR pointing at the wrong wall — walk it again before you trust the list.

action_test.warn: Sirens really sound and messages really send. That is the point: an emergency channel discovered broken during the emergency is what this page exists to prevent. Every run is recorded in the log as a test.
action_test.subtitle: One button per action, and it really runs
action_test.no_profiles: No response profiles yet. Create one under Response profiles.
action_test.no_actions: This profile has no action to test.
action_test.confirm: Really run “{action}” now? It executes for real.

what.camera: Takes the snapshot or the recording
what.delay: Nothing: a delay is the waiting itself

reason.unknown_profile: that response profile no longer exists
reason.no_recipients: nobody left to send it to: every contact it names is disabled, or has no channel
reason.unknown_contact: that contact or channel no longer exists
reason.not_permitted: you do not have the permission to run a test

contacts.title: Contacts
contacts.none: No contacts yet. An escalation reaches people, so it needs at least one.
contacts.channels_hint: Tried highest first. Put the channel that survives a cut internet connection somewhere in the list, not at the bottom.
contacts.service_hint: Any notify service or notify entity in this installation. Foyer orchestrates transports; it does not implement them.
contacts.target_hint: What this transport needs to reach the person: a phone number, a chat id. Leave it empty when the service already knows.
contacts.actionable_hint: The Companion app can; an SMS cannot. A transport throws away a key it does not know without a word, so this is declared rather than guessed.
contacts.quiet_hint: Inside this window only what is loud enough reaches this contact. It never silences the alarm for the whole household.
contacts.quiet_severity_hint: On the log's own scale. Left at alarm, a break-in gets through at four in the morning and a successful arming does not.
contacts.linked_hint: Lets an acknowledgement from this person's phone be attributed to them in the log.
contacts.orchestration: Escalation targets people, not services. Home Assistant already provides the transports, so what is configured here is who, in what order, and when to stop.
contacts.test_after_save: Save the contact first: a test sends through the stored channel, not the draft.
contacts.no_policies: No escalation steps yet. A step is a notification with a time on it, added to a response profile.
contacts.exhausted: If nobody acknowledges, the last step raises escalation_exhausted, which is itself a moment a profile can act on.
contacts.ack_stops: The policy stops the instant any of these arrives. Every acknowledgement records who and through which channel.
contacts.ack_push: Action button in a push notification
contacts.ack_push_how: A channel marked as able to carry one
contacts.ack_disarm_how: Keypad, card, tag, service call — an area the alarm touched
contacts.ack_dtmf: Key press during a voice call
contacts.ack_dtmf_how: Captured by the provider, fed back to the webhook below
contacts.webhook_enable: Accept an acknowledgement from a webhook
contacts.webhook_warning: This URL stops an alarm, and nothing authenticates it.
contacts.webhook_warning_hint: Home Assistant webhooks are open to whoever holds the address: anybody who has it, or intercepts it, can stop the escalation on its way to your neighbour. Switch it on only if a voice provider needs it, and give the address to nothing else.
contacts.webhook_hint: Post to this path from the voice provider when the key is pressed. Switching this off forgets the address: switching it on again gives out a new one.
contacts.actionable_entity: This is a notify entity: it carries a message and a title and nothing else, so no button, no target and no extra data reach the phone. Use the notify service behind it if this channel should be able to acknowledge.

rules.title: Rules
rules.none: No rules yet. The house arms itself only once one exists.
rules.switched_off: Automatic rules are switched off. Nothing will arm or disarm on its own.
rules.trigger_hint_absence: Every person chosen has to be away for the whole time.
rules.trigger_hint_presence: Fires when one of them comes home. Somebody already at home has not arrived.
rules.trigger_hint_time: Happens once. Blocked by a guard, the occurrence is missed rather than postponed.
rules.trigger_hint_entity: The entity has to hold that state for the whole time.
rules.no_people: No person or device tracker entities were found.
rules.people_hint: A person Home Assistant cannot read is never taken as evidence that nobody is in.
rules.window_hint: Outside this window the rule does not exist: it is not blocked and nothing is logged.
rules.guard_ready: Only if every zone is ready
rules.guard_ready_hint: Otherwise the rule would arm around an open window.
rules.guard_quiet_label: Only if no interior motion for (minutes)
rules.guard_quiet_hint: Catches the flat phone battery: somebody is in, their phone is not.
rules.grace_hint: A notification with a Cancel button before it acts. 0 acts at once.
rules.notify_hint: Who hears the countdown and holds the Cancel button. Their quiet hours still apply.
rules.visitor_intro: A named window suspends automatic arming — and in six months the log says why, which a bare suspension never will.
rules.suspension_next_hint: Ends the next time the rule would have acted.
rules.instead_hint: Applied when the suspended rule would have armed, not when the window opens.
rules.disarming_warning: Presence is inferred from a phone. A stolen phone disarms the house, GPS drift of 200 metres disarms the house, a cloned MAC address on the home network disarms the house. This is the most banal attack against a DIY alarm, which is why this is off by default.
rules.allow_disarm_hint: Also covers a scenario switch that would drop an armed area.
rules.perimeter_note: Perimeter areas are excluded in the engine, not on this screen. Whoever walks in on a stolen phone still finds every external door and window armed.
rules.block_not_ready_refused: Refused: a zone was not ready

health.settings_hint: Which entity reports the mains, where the watchdog pings, and which radios are counted together. Changing any of it is a configuration edit.
health.mains_hint: A UPS over NUT or a smart plug already gives you one. If it is also a zone of type technical, it keeps its own alarm and its own acknowledgement — this only tells Foyer which one is the mains.
health.mains_states_hint: Which states mean the mains has failed, separated by commas. A UPS binary sensor is usually “on” for a failure and a power sensor “off”: a wrong answer here is an alarm that never fires.
health.watchdog_off_hint: Nothing outside the house knows whether Foyer is alive
health.watchdog_note: Foyer watches the watchdog too: repeated failures to reach this endpoint are reported here, because being unable to reach the internet means no internet notification would go out either.
health.url_hint: healthchecks.io, Uptime Kuma, Cronitor, or anything that answers. If Home Assistant dies the pings stop and that service raises the alarm — the only answer to a dead system being unable to report its own death.
health.interval_hint: Seconds between pings. Shorter means the outside world learns sooner that Home Assistant has died.
health.failures_hint: How many pings in a row must fail before Foyer says so here.
health.payload: Include the state of the house in the ping
health.payload_warning: A ping that says “armed, nobody home” tells whoever runs that service exactly when your house is empty. Even switched on, Foyer sends only how many areas are armed — never which scenario, which areas, or which zones are open.
health.channels_note: A broken channel is announced through a different one: warning you about a dead channel over the dead channel is the joke that writes itself. Send a test from the Contacts page.
health.no_radios: No radios are configured, so correlated silence is not counted.
health.radios_hint: A radio is one integration's config entry: every zone of one ZHA, Z-Wave JS or Zigbee2MQTT installation shares it, so naming the entry once assigns forty zones.
health.radios_note: Many zones on one radio going quiet within seconds is the signature of jamming — and of a coordinator crash, a firmware update, a channel change and a power cut to a room of mains-powered routers. That is why the event is called suspected.
health.entry_hint: Only integrations that back at least one of your zones.
health.coordinator_hint: The gate that makes this worth having: zones going quiet while the coordinator answers is interference, zones going quiet with the coordinator gone is a dead coordinator. Without one, Foyer raises nothing on this radio rather than guessing.
health.rf_zones_hint: Or 40% of that radio's zones, whichever is lower.
health.rf_confirm_hint: How long the silence must last before Foyer says so. This is what a coordinator reboot and a firmware update walk into instead of the siren.
health.faults_sub: also raised as Home Assistant repair issues
health.diagnostics_hint: An anonymised dump of the configuration and the state: no codes, no hashes, no personal names, no URLs, and entity ids reduced to stable placeholders. It is what turns a bug report into something answerable.
health.diagnostics_where: The download button is Home Assistant's own, on the integration's page, and it is available to administrators.
